nodes.title: TypeNet: Deep Learning Keystroke Biometrics
nodes.dataset: Largest free-text keystroke databases with >136M keystrokes from 168,000 physical keyboard users and 60,000 touchscreen users.
nodes.methodology: LSTM-based deep learning models trained with keystroke sequences, evaluated using different loss functions, sample sizes, and device types (physical vs touchscreen keyboards).
nodes.contribution: Introduces TypeNet, a scalable LSTM model for free-text keystroke authentication; achieves state-of-the-art results; provides cross-device and cross-database generalization.

nodes.title: Covert lie detection using keyboard dynamics
nodes.dataset: 60 participants (40 training, 20 test) with fabricated ID profiles and real personal information.
nodes.methodology: Keystroke dynamics analysis using unexpected questions to reveal deception clues through typing pattern deviations.
nodes.contribution: Novel covert lie detection method using keyboard dynamics instead of mouse tracking for online applications.

nodes.title: Non-Acted Text and Keystrokes Database and Learning Methods to Recognize Emotions
nodes.dataset: Multimodal text-keystrokes dataset with 69 participants, including video-induced stimuli and unguided text reviews.
nodes.methodology: Text-keystroke data is collected from 69 participants via controlled video stimuli. Features are extracted from text and keystrokes, fused with tree-based selection and SVM for emotion classification.
nodes.contribution: Introduces a novel CI-based framework and baseline dataset for emotion recognition in short text, combining text and keystroke features.

nodes.title: The Influence of Emotion on Keyboard Typing: An Experimental Study Using Auditory Stimuli
nodes.dataset: Keystroke data collected from 52 participants under IADS-induced emotional conditions (Valence x Arousal dimensions).
nodes.methodology: Controlled experiment using International Affective Digitized Sounds (IADS) to induce emotional states, followed by two-way ANOVA analysis of keystroke data.
nodes.contribution: Demonstrates arousal influences keystroke duration/latency, suggesting personalized models could enhance emotion recognition accuracy.

nodes.title: DeepMood: Modeling Mobile Phone Typing Dynamics for Mood Detection
nodes.dataset: BiAffect study data from 20 participants (7 bipolar I, 5 bipolar II, 8 controls) with session-level typing metadata and clinical ratings (HDRS/YMRS).
nodes.methodology: Proposes DeepMood, a late fusion deep architecture combining RNNs for multi-view metadata (keypress timing, accelerometer) with interaction modeling across views.
nodes.contribution: 1) Data analysis linking typing patterns to bipolar mood states; 2) Novel two-stage late fusion strategy for multi-view time series; 3) Empirical validation of mobile metadata for mood prediction.
